Where does AI actually belong in HR? How do you know if you need it, and how would you know you can trust it?

Earlier this week, I had the privilege of spending the morning with over 30 HR leaders at our H2O.ai Executive HR Masterclass. Rather than just listen to me talk, I wanted the room to answer those questions themselves, with their laptop, without any coding. The energy in that room carried the whole morning!!!

And that leads to the real question: if AI becomes a resource on your team, who manages it, and who checks its work? For me, that answer is in the heart of democratizing AI. The people who own the judgement should keep owning it.

Being upskilled in AI means knowing where it fits in your own work and building on it. Non-technical teams can do that today, with planning, time and the right guidance. It won't happen in just one morning, but it adds up with every use case you try!

My role has always been about closing the gap between what AI can do and what an organization is ready to trust, and this week that gap felt a little smaller.
